primitives.note: Sigil orb, Distortion impact, Ethereal Chains initial hit, and each Mimic variant's primary damage all resolve on cast/impact on a normal cooldown

Sigil of Malice applies a 3.5s mark on the target; the next damaging ability against that target consumes it for a second, equal-damage instance. Mimic: Sigil of Malice reproduces this orb+mark structure with its own (doubled) values, and per the wiki notes Q and Mimic: Sigil can detonate each other's marks
Ethereal Chains has an initial hit plus a delayed (1.5s later) fracture hit if the tether isn't broken; Mimic: Ethereal Chains mirrors this two-part timing with doubled fracture damage
Mana costs (50/50-100/50) against Leblanc's mana pool can meaningfully cap cast frequency over a 15s fight, especially W scaling up to 100 at rank 5

needsBespoke.why: Mimic's 'copy the last-used basic ability with modified numbers' behavior is a rotation-level branch (which spell was last cast), not a new damage mechanic: each branch (Mimic: Sigil, Mimic: Distortion, Mimic: Ethereal Chains) reduces to the same plain-cast / target-stacks / recast-or-multipart primitives already used by Q, W, and E, just with R's own base/ratio values. The simulator can implement R as 'recast the most recently cast of Q/W/E's primitive shape using R's numbers.'

options: Mimic: Sigil always resolves both the orb hit and the doubled 'mark consumption' hit together as a single guaranteed two-part burst on cast
Mimic: Sigil only deals the orb damage on cast and places a mark; the doubled damage only triggers if LeBlanc's next damaging ability (or an already-marked target) consumes it, exactly like base Q
quotes: {{sbc|Mimic: Sigil of Malice:}} The orb deals modified damage, while the mark consumption deals double that amount.

unsettled.question: If LeBlanc casts Q (marking the target) and then casts R while Mimic defaults to Mimic: Sigil of Malice, does R's orb also consume/detonate the pre-existing Q mark on top of its own orb+mark payout, since the wiki states Sigil and Mimic: Sigil 'can detonate each other's marks'?

options: Tether always survives against a stationary, non-moving dummy target, so both E instances always land
Some other rule (e.g. range-based break) could prevent the fracture even against a stationary target
quotes: If the tether is not broken by the end of its duration, it fractures to deal {{as|magic damage}} to the target and {{tip|root}} them for {{fd|1.5}} seconds

proposal: Open with Q (Sigil of Malice) on the dummy to deal the orb's initial magic damage and apply the 3.5s mark.
Immediately follow with E (Ethereal Chains) so its initial hit is the 'next damaging ability' that consumes Q's mark for the second Q damage instance, plus E's own initial damage.
Hold position through the 1.5s tether window (stationary dummy cannot break it) to collect E's delayed fracture damage.
Cast W (Distortion) onto the dummy for its impact AoE damage as soon as it is off cooldown.

Use R (Mimic) to recast whichever of Q/W/E was most recently cast for a bonus damage instance (prefer recasting immediately after Q or E to interact with marks/tethers, pending the unsettled Mimic-mark-stacking question).
Re-cast Q on its 6s cooldown as the primary filler between W/E cooldowns, letting each subsequent damaging ability consume the fresh mark.
Fill any remaining time with auto-attacks on the dummy while spells are on cooldown.
Repeat the Q → (W or E) → mark-consumption loop for the rest of the 15s window, keeping W and E on cooldown as soon as they're available.
questions: Should R (Mimic) be cast right after Q (for a possible immediate Mimic: Sigil double-mark burst) or right after E (for a guaranteed two-part Mimic: Ethereal Chains), given the unresolved mark-stacking and instant-vs-delayed questions above?

In the 15s fight, is it worth pausing 1.5s to let Ethereal Chains fracture, or does the DPS-optimal line skip waiting and instead keep firing Q/W on cooldown, sacrificing the fracture damage on some casts?

Does the simulator want LeBlanc's auto-attacks included as filler at all, given her weak base AD and no on-hit effects, or should all idle time instead be spent walking up for the next skillshot (not applicable here since there is no positioning cost against a fixed dummy)?
